Position title: Radiocommunications Technician
Work location: Lyndhurst, VIC 3975
Salary: $79,500 - $100,000

Main task: You will be part of a team that will perform project, installation, and maintenance
works - both in workshops and field locations. The range of technologies will include but not be
limited to, underground leaky feeder radio systems, wide area radio networks, fibre optic and
data networks, Wi-Fi, remote control and monitoring systems, microwave systems and general
electronic repairs.

Responsibilities:
- Form part of our clients on site technical team to maintain various Communication &
Network equipment.
- New systems workshop build, programming, and factory acceptance testing.
- On Site Installation, Commissioning and fault finding of Voice & Data Radio systems
predominantly Motorola.
- On Site Installation, Commissioning and fault finding of microwave equipment and
various IP based ancillary equipment.
- On Site Installation, Commissioning and fault finding of Rajant Mesh equipment and
networks.
- On Site Installation, Commissioning and fault finding of communications equipment in a
wide variety of locations, including buildings, towers, mobile plant and vehicles.
- Liaise with key stakeholders to ensure project delivery is completed as per design, within
budget, and schedule expectations.
- Completion of Preventative Maintenance Inspections of customer equipment when due.
- Complete Project documentation, Survey reports, FAT and SAT documentation where
required.
- Provide technical input to support sales where required.
- Ensure all activities undertaken are carried out in accordance with company safety and
quality policies and procedures.
- Participate in a 24/7 on call roster on call support for specified customers to meet
contractual SLA’s.

To be suitable for this position you require the following:
- Holder of a diploma or any relevant qualification
- At least 2 years of relevant work experience
- Interest in RF, Electronics, ICT, Networking and various other Technologies.
- Sound written and verbal communication skills.
- Self-motivation and excellent time management skills.
- Ability to learn new information quickly.
- Intermediate to advanced computer literacy.
- Willingness to travel for extended periods of time within VIC and interstate.
- A good understanding and commitment to safety

Our client is a highly regarded developer and builder with a strong reputation for delivering landmark residential and mixed-use developments across Queensland. With a strong pipeline of upcoming projects and continued business growth, they are seeking an experienced Senior Contracts Administrator to join their Brisbane team. 
 This is an excellent opportunity to work on large-scale luxury apartment developments valued between $170 million and $200 million, taking ownership of the commercial function from pre-contract through to project delivery. 
  Key Responsibilities:  
 
 Lead procurement, tendering, and management of subcontract packages through to final account. 
 Administer subcontract agreements, variations, progress claims, and contract correspondence. 
 Assess and manage subcontractor claims and payment schedules. 
 Monitor project costs, forecasting, budgets, and monthly financial reporting. 
 Manage head contract administration and commercial risk. 
 Maintain accurate project records and ensure contractual compliance. 
 Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, consultants, subcontractors, and internal stakeholders. 
 
  Experience Required:  
 
 Proven experience as a Senior Contracts Administrator or a highly capable Contracts Administrator ready to step into a senior position. 
 Qualifications in Construction Management, Quantity Surveying, Commercial Management, or a related discipline. 
 Experience delivering large-scale residential, commercial, or mixed-use construction projects. 
 Strong commercial acumen with excellent attention to detail. 
 Well-developed stakeholder management and communication skills. 
 Experience using construction management and project administration software. 
 Ability to thrive in a fast-paced project environment while managing competing priorities.

Work type: Part time

Located in: Adelaide CBD

Categories: Nursing-Midwifery




 

Women's and Children's Health Network, Network Operations Centre, North Adelaide 5006

Salary - RN-M3, $130,190.00 - $136,010.00 + 12% Superannuation and Salary Sacrifice Benefits

Part Time (0.74FTE), Ongoing-Permanent

About WCHN
Join the Women's and Children's Health Network (WCHN), South Australia's leading provider of care for women, babies, children and young people. We're shaping the future of healthcare through compassion, innovation and excellence - with our communities at the heart of everything we do.

What WCHN Can Offer You

Access to salary packaging benefits of up to $9,010 each FBT year for living expenses (e.g. mortgage, rent, utilities, groceries), plus an additional $2,650 each FBT year for meal entertainment expenses.

Access to Fitness Passport (workplace health and fitness program that gives you and your family access to a wide choice of gyms and pools across South Australia.)

Free public transport to and from the Women's and Children's Hospital for SA Health metropolitan hospital staff (excludes network community sites.

Support for you and your family via our Employee Assistance Program.

Relocation financial support may be negotiated, subject to eligibility. Click here for details and contact the enquires person for further information.

About the role

The Nurse Manager provides direct clinical oversight to the permanent pool and AIN's-AIM's and holds an educational portfolio across the Network Operations Centre. The Nurse Manager assesses the skills and competencies of the permanent pool staff and AIN's-AIM's and supports increasing their knowledge and versatility through education and development activities.

Key duties of the role

Integrate contemporary information and evidence with personal experience to support decision making, innovative thinking, and objective analysis.

Maintain productive working relationships and manage conflict resolution.

Ensure mechanisms are in place to support ongoing education where work and learning are integrated.

Change local processes and practices in accordance with emerging management needs, evaluation results, and imminent systems problems.

Contribute to the development of, implementation of, and monitoring of corporate policies and processes.

Skills and Experience

Registered or eligible for registration as a Nurse-Midwife with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia and who holds, or who is eligible to hold, a current practicing certificate.

Registered Nurse-Midwife with at least 3 years post-registration experience.

Demonstrated experience in management and leadership roles.

Demonstrated ability in the leadership and facilitation of change management.

Effective leadership skills, including highly developed skills in communication and problem solving.
